Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

victim noun

of a crime, a wrong, an accident

also victims, the injured party, fall victim to, be a victim of

classical

Cic. Div. Caec. 60: injūriam accipere ab aliquō (Lewis & Short, s.v. injūria)

is quī injūriam accēpit

phrase: a relative clause with injūria, injūriae f. and accipiō

the one who has been wronged

Classical Latin has no single word for the victim of a crime: it names the person by what was done, in a relative clause or a participle: is cui injūria facta est, quī spoliātus est (robbed), quī circumventus est (cheated), quī in eō cāsū periērunt (the victims of an accident).

Other words

  • victima, victimae f. — a beast for sacrifice

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical · Caes. B.G. 6.16 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 2.61: sē victimam reī pūblicae praebēre · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically an animal offered in sacrifice, and figuratively someone who gives himself up as an offering (Cic. Fin. 2.61). Using it for the victim of a crime or an accident follows the modern languages.

Examples

  • Quid tibi injūriae factum est?

    What have they done to you?Fōrm. XVI 49 (Franmōrārius, 2013)

See also crime, criminal, hurt, murder.
